text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 144:
A system of crossed levers, termed “Lazy Tongs.” A short alternating rectilinear motion of rod at the right will give a similar but much greater motion to rod at the left.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 144; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_144.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 385:
Contrivance employed in Russia for shutting doors. One pin is fitted to and turns in socket attached to door, and the other is similarly attached to frame. In opening the door, pins are brought together, and weight is raised. Weight closes door by depressing the joint of the toggle toward a straight line, and so widening the space between the pins.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 385; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_385.html.

text:
Henry T. Brown (1908), movement 387:
The steps are pivoted at one edge into wooden bars forming string-pieces, and their other edge is supported by rods suspended from bars forming hand-rails. The steps remain horizontal whatever position the ladder assumes.
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 387; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_387.html.
